building.name: Bank of Canton
building.completed_conflict: The city's Modern & Postmodern styles context statement dates this building 1984; the assessor's roll records it as built 1985.

historical_record.description: A building put up here in 1849 held private assaying, smelting and minting works until 1851, was leased to the United States Assay Office from 1851 to 1853, and was bought by the government late in 1853 and made San Francisco's first United States Branch Mint.
The mint building was turned into the United States Sub-Treasury in 1874, the quarters proved unworkable, and it was pulled down the same year.

A four-storey building went up on this site between 1875 and 1877 to house the Sub-Treasury, and it survives inside the tower as City Landmark No. 34: about sixty feet square and 7,200 square feet in all, restored as the Pacific Heritage Museum to designs by Charles Hall Page and Associates, keeping its coin vault, a decorative column, its steel beam and corrugated iron floor system and its interior brick walls.

unknowns: The 2025 assessor's roll dates this parcel 1985, which is the headquarters tower built around the restored Sub-Treasury.
